root_cause.text: In the DWC3 gadget driver, `dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw()` could invoke `power_supply_set_property()` directly from atomic context, but the power-supply/PMIC path may sleep, so the callback violated context rules and could trigger a kernel panic.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says `dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw()` “can be called from atomic context” and “invokes power-supply-core APIs” whose PMIC operations “may sleep”; the patch fixes this by moving the actual `power_supply_set_property(...INPUT_CURRENT_LIMIT...)` call into a new `dwc3_vbus_draw_work()` workqueue handler and changing `dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw()` to only store `current_limit` and `schedule_work()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add workqueue-based programming of the USB power supply input current limit to enforce the controller’s configured VBUS draw.
intent_record.what: A new static workqueue callback, `dwc3_vbus_draw_work()`, was added. It retrieves the parent `struct dwc3` from `work_struct`, initializes a `power_supply_propval`, converts `dwc->current_limit` from mA to µA by multiplying by 1000, and calls `power_supply_set_property()` on `dwc->usb_psy` with `POWER_SUPPLY_PROP_INPUT_CURRENT_LIMIT`. If the call fails, it logs a debug message with the error and current limit.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this adds an asynchronous path for programming the USB power supply's input current limit based on the controller's current limit. This enables the driver to request the intended VBUS draw from the power subsystem and provides debug visibility if setting that limit fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the VBUS draw work item when obtaining the USB power supply so it can be scheduled safely later.
intent_record.what: A call to INIT_WORK(&dwc->vbus_draw_work, dwc3_vbus_draw_work) was added just before returning usb_psy in dwc3_get_usb_power_supply().
intent_record.how: This initializes the dwc->vbus_draw_work work item with its handler before the power supply is used later, allowing deferred work related to VBUS draw to be scheduled safely at runtime instead of operating on an uninitialized work structure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending vbus_draw_work before releasing usb_psy during DWC3 removal to avoid use-after-free races.
intent_record.what: The remove path in dwc3_core_remove() was changed so that when dwc->usb_psy is present, it now enters a braced block, calls cancel_work_sync(&dwc->vbus_draw_work), and then calls power_supply_put(dwc->usb_psy).
intent_record.how: This ensures any pending or running vbus_draw_work is fully synchronized and canceled before the USB power supply reference is released during device removal, preventing the work item from running after associated resources have been freed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document the new vbus draw work and current limit fields in dwc3_glue_ops.
intent_record.what: Two new kernel-doc comment lines were added to the dwc3_glue_ops structure documentation: one for a vbus_draw_work field described as work to set the VBUS drawing limit, and one for a current_limit field described as the amount of current to draw from VBUS in milliamperes.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior; it only updates the structure documentation to describe two additional members, improving code readability and maintainability for the DWC3 glue layer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add per-controller state for VBUS draw work scheduling and current-limit tracking.
intent_record.what: Two new members were added to `struct dwc3`: a `struct work_struct vbus_draw_work` and an `unsigned int current_limit`, inserted after the existing `usb_psy` pointer.
intent_record.how: This extends the controller state with storage for deferred VBUS draw handling and a cached current-limit value, enabling the driver to track and process USB power/current changes asynchronously.

intent_record.what: In `dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw()`, the local declarations `union power_supply_propval val = {0};` and `int ret;` were removed from the function body.
intent_record.how: This change has no direct runtime effect by itself; it eliminates two unused local variables from the function, leaving the existing USB2 PHY power-setting path unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer USB VBUS current-limit updates to workqueue context by recording the requested limit and scheduling work instead of setting the power-supply property synchronously.
intent_record.what: In dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw(), the code no longer converts mA to a power-supply property value and calls power_supply_set_property() directly. Instead, it stores the requested mA value in dwc->current_limit, schedules dwc->vbus_draw_work, and unconditionally returns 0 after the existing usb_psy presence check.
intent_record.how: This changes VBUS current draw handling from a synchronous direct power-supply update to an asynchronous deferred work item. The requested current limit is now applied later by worker context, which can avoid doing the power-supply operation in the immediate call path and ensures the requested value is persisted for the work handler to process.

grouping_result.intent: Defer USB VBUS current-limit updates to workqueue context by recording the requested limit and scheduling work instead of setting the power-supply property synchronously.
Cancel pending vbus_draw_work before releasing usb_psy during DWC3 removal to avoid use-after-free races.
Document the new vbus draw work and current limit fields in dwc3_glue_ops.
Add per-controller state for VBUS draw work scheduling and current-limit tracking.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause by deferring dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw() power-supply updates out of atomic context into workqueue context, avoiding the sleep-in-atomic bug that could panic the kernel.

The root cause is calling power_supply_set_property() from atomic context in dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw(), but this change only cancels pending vbus_draw_work before freeing usb_psy during removal to prevent a use-after-free race. It does not address the atomic-context sleep violation.

This change only documents new vbus draw work/current limit fields in dwc3_glue_ops. It does not modify the atomic-context call to power_supply_set_property(), nor address the sleep-in-atomic bug in dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw().

The change adds per-controller work scheduling for VBUS draw handling, which directly relates to the unsafe direct call from atomic context. Deferring VBUS/power-supply interaction to scheduled work is a plausible fix for the sleep-in-atomic-context issue.

This change only removes unused local variables in dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw() and does not address the atomic-context call to power_supply_set_property() or the sleep-in-atomic bug described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This directly performs the power-supply update synchronously from dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw(), which can be invoked in atomic context. Since power_supply_set_property() may sleep through the PMIC/power-supply path, this statement is the immediate cause of the context-violation bug.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly calls into the power-supply subsystem from dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw(), which can run in atomic context. Because power_supply_set_property() may sleep, invoking it here violates context rules and can trigger a kernel panic.
